```{=html}
<div class="resource-page start-page">
  <section class="resource-hero" aria-labelledby="start-title">
  <div>
  <p class="eyebrow">STT-1100</p>
  <h1 id="start-title">Start the course</h1>
  <p>STT-1100 works as a data science pathway. Each module begins with a concrete situation, places you in a professional role, and leads to something visible: a report, an analysis, a visualization, a function or a dashboard.</p>
  <div class="resource-actions" aria-label="Quick links">
  <a class="home-action home-action--primary" href="modules.html">View modules</a>
  <a class="home-action" href="boite_outils.html">Toolbox</a>
  <a class="home-action" href="ressources.html">Resources</a>
  </div>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-panel" aria-label="Pathway landmarks">
  <div><span>01</span><p>Read the learning plan</p></div>
  <div><span>02</span><p>Enter the adventure</p></div>
  <div><span>03</span><p>Complete the challenge</p></div>
  <div><span>04</span><p>Consolidate with exercises</p></div>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="philosophy-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="philosophy-title">Course philosophy</h2>
  <p>You learn data science by producing, explaining and revising your own work.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="principle-grid">
  <article class="principle-card"><h3>Understand before automating</h3><p>Code is used to answer a question. Before looking for the perfect function, identify the variables, context, units and expected deliverable.</p></article>
  <article class="principle-card"><h3>Work reproducibly</h3><p>Quarto reports, R scripts and GitHub repositories keep the reasoning trace. A result should be reproducible, reviewable and explainable.</p></article>
  <article class="principle-card"><h3>Build careful interpretation</h3><p>A useful analysis is more than a graph or model. It states what the data support and what they do not allow you to conclude.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="plan-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="plan-title">How a module works</h2>
  <p>Each module homepage presents the learning plan as expandable cards.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">1</span><h3>Readings</h3><p>The readings provide words, concepts and functions to recognize. They prepare the adventure rather than replacing practice.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">2</span><h3>Adventure</h3><p>The adventure is the main immersion. You play a data science role and follow a guided situation, often longer.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">3</span><h3>Challenge</h3><p>The challenge turns guided practice into a personal production. It is the short deliverable showing what you can do in the module.</p></article>
  <article class="flow-card"><span class="flow-number">4</span><h3>Exercises</h3><p>The exercises stabilize technical moves: importing, transforming, visualizing, diagnosing, interpreting and rendering work.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="immersion-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="immersion-title">Data science immersion</h2>
  <p>The modules place you in realistic roles. The goal is not only to learn R commands, but to think like someone who turns data into decisions.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="role-grid">
  <article class="role-card"><h3>Analyst</h3><p>Explore a table, choose useful summaries and explain what appears important.</p></article>
  <article class="role-card"><h3>Data developer</h3><p>Clean, connect and document files so they become usable.</p></article>
  <article class="role-card"><h3>Communicator</h3><p>Turn an analysis into a graph, report or dashboard that others can understand.</p></article>
  <article class="role-card"><h3>Critical reviewer</h3><p>Identify limits, biases, fragile code and conclusions that go too far.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="tools-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="tools-title">Tools to install</h2>
  <p>These tools form the course's minimal environment.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid compact-hub">
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>R</h3><p>The language used to import, transform, visualize and analyze data.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://www.r-project.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>R Project</span><span>Official download.</span></a></div></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>RStudio</h3><p>The working environment used to write code, manage projects and produce reports.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>RStudio Desktop</span><span>Download from Posit.</span></a></div></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Quarto</h3><p>The system that turns.qmd files into HTML reports, notes and web pages.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Quarto getting started</span><span>Installation and first document.</span></a></div></article>
  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Git and GitHub</h3><p>Version-control tools used to track changes and submit some work.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://git-scm.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Git</span><span>Local installation.</span></a><a href="https://docs.github.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>GitHub Docs</span><span>Official documentation.</span></a></div></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="routine-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="routine-title">Minimal routine</h2>
  <p>Each work session should follow a simple routine. It reduces errors and keeps the project reproducible.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>Open the right project in RStudio.</li>
  <li>Read the learning-plan card linked to the work of the day.</li>
  <li>Run code in small sections and check outputs.</li>
  <li>Render the Quarto document to catch errors.</li>
  <li>Keep only useful files, then commit if the module asks for it.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Help during the course">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>When stuck</h3><p>Reproduce the error, read the full message, then isolate the smallest possible example.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>With the course AI assistant</h3><p>Ask for an explanation, a check or a debugging lead. Always verify the answer before using it.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Before submitting</h3><p>Render the file, reread the conclusions and check that the deliverable answers the challenge.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>
</div>
```
